close_reason: No-op resolution: defense of the existing resolve_args two-phase atomic design. The pattern (collect references read-only, validate all, then mutate) is preserved. Closing as a no-op; the defended shape stays.
description:
Why this choice is correct: resolve_args (crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:131-195) collects all ResultReferences into a Vec, validates EVERY one read-only, and only then mutates args. If any single reference fails, args is returned byte-for-byte unchanged. This is enforced by tests at parse.rs:404-421 (resolve_args_atomic_on_partial_failure) and reasserted at lines 365-389 for individual error paths.

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing: 1) Single-pass apply-as-you-go: walk and mutate args in place, returning Err on the first failed reference. Pros (simpler code) lose to cons (args is now half-mutated; a retry against the same args would behave differently from the original call). The atomic shape preserves the JMAP idempotency contract — a client retrying a request after a transient error sees identical behaviour. 2) Optimistic apply with rollback: mutate, on error undo. Adds complexity and a new bug class (rollback that fails). The Vec<resolution> staging buffer is small (bounded by obj.len()) and the allocation is the right tradeoff.

The pattern is unusual in async Rust code because mutation under error-recovery feels expensive — but the borrow-checker forces the read-only pass anyway (cannot iterate obj while mutating obj), so we get atomicity essentially for free. Defensible explicitly because reviewer reflex is "two passes is slow" — the answer is "we are already paying for two passes by construction".
title: Two-phase atomic resolve_args — args unchanged on partial failure
